experiment: E2 rerun: runtime-invoked inherited skill and premature-finish guard
motivation: E1 (one replicate, exploratory arm) found that a skill offered as a tool was almost never called, while the runtime invoking it raised success from 3/8 to 6/8. LFM2.5 mostly failed by ending turns with a plan and no tool call. This rerun tests both effects on new tasks with seeds, with the analysis fixed in advance.

arms.guard: tools + premature-finish guard: a final answer given before any successful edit or command is returned to the model once
arms.controller: the runtime runs skill_run_tests before the first turn and after every successful edit and hands the model the structured result

task_provenance: Written by the experimenter (Opus) after E1 finished and before any E2 run; disjoint from E1 tasks, skill dev cases and held-out admission cases; the skill was not run on them before the experiment.
runs: 2 agents x 3 seeds x 4 tasks x 4 arms = 96; one model loaded at a time; arms interleaved within each task
outcome_judge: bench/run_bench.py after the agent finishes: protected tests byte-identical AND the task verifier passes (pytest 8.3.5 in a private venv, node --test, or unittest).
unit_of_analysis: paired unit = (agent, task, seed); 24 units per arm comparison

primary_hypothesis.test: count units where controller succeeds and none fails (wins) and the reverse (losses); exact one-sided sign test on wins vs losses

secondary_hypotheses.H_G: guard beats none (same test and thresholds)
secondary_hypotheses.H_GC: both beats controller (same test and thresholds); a rejection means the guard adds nothing on top of the controller

descriptive_only: total executor actions including runtime test runs
known_threats: The controller arms receive runtime test executions that do not count against the model's 20 steps; total actions and wall time are reported so the extra compute is visible.
Four small synthetic tasks written by the same experimenter who wrote the brief, the skill brief and the arms.
Seeds vary sampling only; llama.cpp Metal is not bit-exact across runs.
The skill author (Opus) is far stronger than the receiving models.
